videoAttributeViewModel.subtitle:
In the context of programming languages, memory safety refers to the prevention of certain types of errors that can occur when a program accesses memory. Rust is a memory-safe language, which means that it has built-in mechanisms to prevent these errors from occurring.

One common type of memory safety error is a buffer overflow, which occurs when a program writes more data to a buffer than it is supposed to. This can lead to the corruption of other data in memory, or even to the execution of arbitrary code. Rust prevents buffer overflows by using a type system that enforces strict rules about how memory can be accessed.
